name: BattlePresentation_UploadTileVariant
notes: The readable candidate decrements and bounds the selected tile variant, then writes a 32-byte source, VRAM destination, and fixed DMA control value.

The reference keeps that computed source in the first transfer register and emits one restored-writeback three-word DMA transfer. The current canonical source keeps the index in r3 and emits three scalar stores.

Bounded ordinary-C aggregate trials either retained the scalar-store result (60 bytes, 27 differing halfwords) or introduced a 12-byte stack aggregate and block copy (68 bytes, 31 differing halfwords). Two inline helper argument orderings remained 60 bytes and retained scalar stores.

No compiler-route change, inline assembly, fixed-register variable, barrier, ABI escape, copied instruction bytes, or external source was used. Retained assembly remains authoritative and this draft claims zero DONE bytes.

2026-08-27: reclassified measured-draft -> proven-permanent. This owner's retained assembly is already independently proven unreachable from ordinary C at the manifest/classification level: out/gs1-en/full/asm/manifest.json marks it kind=thumb_multiple_transfer_module, retention starting with keep_, confidence=proven, citing arm_md/arm_c line ranges showing GCC 2.96's Thumb backend can only emit a multi-register stmia paired immediately with a matching ldmia (movmem8b/movmem12b), and that ARM's standalone store_multiple/stmsi patterns are TARGET_ARM only -- a lone stmia from independently-computed register values (as this owner's reference has) is architecturally unreachable on this route, not an unexplored search space. This specific pattern was independently rediscovered by multiple dedicated passes this session (08004838, 0800bc48, 08003e10, 0808fecc, 080c0184, and partially 080e7404) before the shared manifest-level proof was found; recording the status correction here so future sessions don't repeat the rediscovery.
